# March Basketball Under the Lottery Reform: Who Rests and Who Plays

<sub>Proposed by the synthesis, not on the user's list.</sub>

**Summary.** The lottery reform should mean less tanking and fewer shutdowns in March, so our playoffs (weeks 19 to 21, ending 2027-03-28) should look more normal than last year's. The risk does not go away. Watch teams that are out of the race with nothing to play for, teams locked into a seed, and teams that do not own their pick, where the experts disagree. Do not build March plans on last season's late numbers from tanking teams.

## What the lottery reform changes

Several experts expect the new anti-tanking lottery rules to make March more competitive across most of the league. Fewer teams should tank, so there will be fewer cheap wins against tanking teams. One expert counted about eight or nine teams tanking or resting players during last season's fantasy playoffs. He expects this season to be less extreme. ([09-26](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=140), [08-21](https://youtu.be/uRsfijpBPok?t=164), [08-27](https://youtu.be/ZAyie8lKyYc?t=2299), [07-14](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=144))

The key mechanism is a relegation zone. Finishing in the bottom three is now a penalty. With top-protected picks under the new odds, a bottom-three finish can give a worse chance at a top-two pick than finishing 4th to 10th. So bottom teams have a reason to win games. One expert also calls the 2027 draft weak, which further reduces the pull to tank. ([07-31](https://youtu.be/oEywzBZfAvY?t=812), [07-13](https://youtu.be/Rqb5GdrSweY?t=592), [07-13](https://youtu.be/Rqb5GdrSweY?t=275), [07-20](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=1296))

This is why our playoff end date of March 28 makes sense. One expert now suggests ending head-to-head playoffs on March 28 instead of March 21. Another says leagues can end a week later than before because there should be less late-season resting. He also expects a smaller late-season spike in injuries because there should be fewer fake injuries. One analyst goes further and expects every team to keep trying in March and April in the current parity era. ([09-21](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=2141), [08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=372), [08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1889), [08-20](https://youtu.be/s28HvC2grAk?t=1816))

## Teams that still rest or shut down players

Less tanking does not mean no tanking. Once a team decides to tank, injured players may be shut down for the rest of the season even if they could have returned. Tanking teams also pull players after three quarters and sit them for much of March. For us, a player on a confirmed tanking team in late February is a sell candidate before the trade deadline of 2027-03-04. ([08-17](https://youtu.be/LcZcvk8s1xQ?t=890), [07-23](https://youtu.be/UTE0dNIv8nY?t=2196))

Good teams can rest players too. A team locked into a seed has no reason to rush injured players back. In a deep conference the reward for chasing a top seed is smaller, so teams may rest more. A deep conference also removes some easy wins against tanking teams, which makes resting riskier. Late in the season some teams may also play to win or lose for a certain seed or better lottery odds. In March, check the standings each week. Flag any team whose seed can no longer move, and treat its injured stars as day-to-day risks, not locks. ([08-22](https://youtu.be/LXZLrL90crE?t=1062), [08-13](https://youtu.be/okN3fbHJtlA?t=768), [08-13](https://youtu.be/okN3fbHJtlA?t=1997), [08-27](https://youtu.be/ZAyie8lKyYc?t=2337))

The quiet middle is a third risk. A team with no reason to lose and no reason to win in March can cut veteran minutes to develop young players. Factor that into what you pay for its veterans at the auction, and again when you trade for them in February. ([09-26](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=220))

## Teams without their own pick: the experts disagree

The experts split on teams that do not control their own pick. One side says these teams have no reason to tank and no downside either, so they may rest players, be extra careful with injuries, or give young players development minutes late in the season. The Nets, Bucks, Clippers, Pelicans and Mavericks are named, with Brooklyn and Milwaukee as the main examples. Another note adds that they may still give minutes to young players to see what they have, though they have less reason to fake injuries. The other side says these teams have no reason to sit players or to finish bottom three, so they keep pushing to win. In that view their veterans keep their roles and their young players get fewer development minutes. ([08-21](https://youtu.be/uRsfijpBPok?t=1851), [07-13](https://youtu.be/Rqb5GdrSweY?t=1333), [07-14](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=127), [09-14](https://youtu.be/LM0cRCGoAUQ?t=1662), [08-10](https://youtu.be/sfCe7fS9daM?t=1711), [07-20](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=1321), [08-22](https://youtu.be/KLogvUwv_d8?t=1252))

Dallas shows the split clearly. One note lists the Mavericks among teams that may rest players. Another says teams like Dallas, with top-protected picks under the new odds, may push harder to win. Our approach: do not apply a blanket discount to these teams on draft day. Watch their minutes in February. If veterans' minutes drop or injured players stay out longer than expected, sell before 2027-03-04. ([08-21](https://youtu.be/uRsfijpBPok?t=1851), [07-13](https://youtu.be/Rqb5GdrSweY?t=592))

## Young players and rookies in March

Do not count on late-season shutdowns giving rookies big minutes in March. That may not happen much anymore. With less tanking, the usual late-season jump in rookie value may be smaller. In our 12-team league with 144 players drafted, do not spend a bench slot at the auction on a rookie whose case depends on a March role. ([06-25](https://youtu.be/lOshTzDA4SA?t=414), [09-03](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=656))

Some young players still get minutes. Rebuilding teams that are not playoff threats give young players more chances because they want to find out what they have. Young players on rebuilding teams are fairly safe from random rest days, but injuries can still change things. On thin non-playoff teams, an injury to a main player makes the depth a problem and changes the value of the players left. In March, use FAB and the 6 weekly adds on young players whose minutes have actually risen. Do not add on a hoped-for shutdown. ([08-18](https://youtu.be/FxaSnyk9g90?t=489), [08-17](https://youtu.be/LcZcvk8s1xQ?t=2097), [08-18](https://youtu.be/FxaSnyk9g90?t=147))

## Why late-season numbers from tanking teams mislead

Be careful with March stats from rebuilding teams. They are hard to trust. Tanking teams pull players early and sit them for much of the month, so the minutes and the box scores do not reflect a normal role. Late-season games are also skewed by tanking, which inflates good teams' results against weak opponents. When you check last season's splits before the auction, do not treat a big March line on a tanking team as a new baseline, and do not treat a quiet March for a star on a tanking team as a decline. ([07-23](https://youtu.be/UTE0dNIv8nY?t=1092), [07-23](https://youtu.be/UTE0dNIv8nY?t=2196), [07-30](https://youtu.be/TiiaNZCJNs8?t=2214))

This season's environment is also different. Fewer teams should finish with very low win totals, and win projections should bunch closer together. One expert says bad teams that used to win about 17 games may now win about 24 because they will play their regular players late. Good teams should win fewer games and should not expect easy wins against bad teams in March. So last year's March patterns are a poor guide for both sides. ([07-21](https://youtu.be/EB1Z_6n56-o?t=2203), [07-21](https://youtu.be/EB1Z_6n56-o?t=2211), [08-10](https://youtu.be/sfCe7fS9daM?t=1675), [08-19](https://youtu.be/2mxpEpGU3H8?t=1858))

## Stars on bad teams at the auction

The experts disagree here too. One says ranges for stars on bad teams should include risk, not just per-game value, because bad teams may rest stars and cut their minutes. Another says not to worry about a team tanking when drafting a good player from that team. Given the reform, our middle path for the 2026-10-18 auction is to bid close to per-game value but stop a few USD short of full price. Plan to move the player before 2027-03-04 if his team starts cutting his minutes. ([09-30](https://youtu.be/MUbNYdjpUDM?t=372), [09-24](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=723))
